lead_headline: Restaurant tracker adds 5 verified leads—Ephemeral Tap & Bottle expands to Jefferson Park, Le Macaron claims Denver Pavilions—while foreclosures climb 6% to 82 weekly filings

restaurant.blurb: 5 new leads today (3 openings, 2 closures) push active inventory to 82 cases (41 openings, 41 closures)—Thursday's batch marks week's strongest daily haul. Openings: Ephemeral Tap & Bottle plants second flag in Jefferson Park (confidence 9, owner Weston Scott's LoHi sibling already operational); Le Macaron French Pastries claims Denver Pavilions downtown (confidence 8, national franchise's first metro location post-fall '24 permitting); China BBQ recycles 3041 W 92nd Westminster slot (confidence 7, fourth tenant since Thousand Wok). Closures concentrate in Federal Boulevard corridor: 7-Eleven at 5090 Federal shutters after 11-year run, property now listed for lease. April's opening three days: +9 net leads (+3.0/day) vs March's +0.7 daily average—seasonal acceleration confirmed or database backlog clearing pending Friday's close.

foreclosure.blurb: 82 filings this week climb 6% from prior week's 77 with zero properties breaching $2M threshold—top case caps at $1.1M Douglas County (14247 Beebalm Loop) as 95 auctions queue for next 7 days.

liquor.blurb: Zero applications today—April 3 extends statewide filing blackout to 34 consecutive days, now 183% beyond December 2024's 12-day record. Database-lag theory hardens: no social chatter, no regulatory announcements, suggesting 60-80 application backlog awaiting system restoration. If Monday delivers fourth straight zero, escalate to Liquor Enforcement Division—12,316-case archive shows no precedent for month-plus void during non-holiday periods.

reputation.blurb: 3 mentions today lift weekly total to 64 citations (+10% vs prior week's 58)—Thursday's haul includes Richmond BizSense CRE roundup pickup, Denver Post church-theater purchase coverage, Instagram A&W closure reshare. Instagram leads weekly sources (16 mentions) edging Denver Post (14), reversing Tuesday's traditional-media dominance as social platforms (Instagram, Facebook, X) command 47% weekly share. Rolling 30-day average climbs to 57 mentions/week as April's first three days match March's 3.2/day opening pace.

subscriptions.blurb: Net −4 yesterday (1 new, 5 canceled) drags MTD to −3 (−1.5/day) as April stumbles out the gate—90-day net holds +129 despite week's bruising. Three-day April start: +1 net (11 new, 10 canceled, 1.0 net/day) vs March's opening trio (+8 net, 2.7/day), signaling 63% acquisition slowdown. Churn accelerates: past 7 days post +6 net (21 new, 15 canceled, 71% retention) vs prior week's +24 (32 new, 8 canceled, 80% retention). Longer view: YTD +128 (+1.4/day) still cushions MTD's −1.5 stumble, but April needs +18 net by month-end to match Q1's pace—current trajectory delivers −12 if trend persists.
